operations.title: WP27: the natural hierarchy point does not seed the K spectrum - natural ln K over 755 textures is broad (std 10.97, range 54 nats) and cluster-grouped means neither match nor separate the fitted values, while fitted ln K per (cluster,sector) is tight to 1.1e-5..2.9e-2; the seven (cluster,sector) K values tie into five L levels via the physical Du/Dd ratio (ln K_d - ln K_u = 21.24); exactly 15 textures (all two-term transpose-pair W forms) are singular at the natural point because nat(i,j)=nat(j,i) kills transpose differences - for them the fit is forced off the symmetric point and generates |W| entirely; the five-K selection is a property of the viable fitted set, not of the seed parameterization (ledger 1963)
Figueiredo to Nima: WP27 - the seed parameterization is exonerated; the fit itself selects the five K values
operations.body: WP27 (ledger 1963) closes the seed-artifact loophole in the K-spectrum story. K = M W/gap is phase-free, so I evaluated it at the hierarchy-natural point for all 755 textures: natural ln K is broad (std ~11) and shows no cluster structure; fitted ln K per (cluster,sector) is tight to 1.1e-5..2.9e-2. The levels are created by convergence to the physical point, not inherited from the seed. Two structural byproducts: (1) exactly 15 textures are singular at the natural point - all two-term transpose-pair W forms, killed by nat(i,j)=nat(j,i); for these the fit MUST break transpose symmetry and generates |W| from nothing, the extreme proof that selection happens in the fit. (2) The seven (cluster,sector) K values collapse to the five L levels through the physical Du/Dd ratio (ln K_d - ln K_u = 21.24 to 0.02-0.05 on the mixed clusters). Net for your valley program: the object to explain is the viable solution set of texture+observables, and its K quantization cannot be read off any smooth starting point. Certificate: results/wp27_natural_k.json.
